stemBlocks.value: On a map a school is at S(-2, 1) and a clinic at C(4, 5). One coordinate unit represents 2 km. (a) Calculate the straight-line distance from the school to the clinic, giving the answer to 3 significant figures. (b) A proposed bus stop is halfway between S and C. Determine its coordinates.
Think first: Work in grid units first and convert to kilometres only at the very end.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p129-q07 from workbook page 129.

solutionSteps.instruction: Convert to kilometres using the scale.
Find the midpoint of S(-2, 1) and C(4, 5).

strategyBlocks.value: Use the distance formula to get SC in coordinate units, multiply by 2 km per unit and round to 3 significant figures; then use the midpoint formula for the bus stop.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) 14.4 km (to 3 significant figures)  (b) The bus stop is at (1, 3).

whyThisWorks.value: A map scale multiplies every real length by the same factor, so the shape of the calculation never changes — you find the length in grid units and scale once at the end. The midpoint formula averages the coordinates because the halfway point sits half of the horizontal step and half of the vertical step along from the start, and averaging does exactly that.

commonErrors.misconception: Doubling the coordinates first and then applying the distance formula, which double-counts the scale if done carelessly.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Doubling the coordinates first and then applying the distance formula, which double-counts the scale if done carelessly.

commonErrors.misconception: Rounding √52 to 7.2 before multiplying, which loses accuracy in the third significant figure.
